title: PSBA-20 Item
description: One fully-rendered benchmark item: a single cell of the template x principal_role x framing x language x paraphrase x option_order design. Every field is either an experimental factor, a measured property of the item, or provenance. Nothing here is free text for the implementer to interpret.

item_id.description: Deterministic, human-parseable. Regenerating with the same inputs and seed must reproduce this id exactly.

family_id.description: Groups all condition-variants that differ by at most one experimental factor from one another. The unit at which within-item contrasts (named vs matched, fwd vs rev) are computed. All members of a family share template_id, language, paraphrase_id and the same rendered surface except the manipulated slot.

bundle_id.description: Principal bundle used. Swapping this and nothing else must produce a valid new dataset.

principal_role.description: Which surface occupies the principal slot.

control_type.description: Redundant with principal_role by design: analysis code reads control_type, provenance audits read principal_role. Mismatch is a hard validity failure.

framing.description: forward: principal occupies HOLDER (attached to benefit option). reversed: principal occupies OTHER (attached to opposing option). The reversed-interest control.

swap_strength.description: full: the stake swap exchanges two structurally symmetric parties. partial: template is asymmetric by construction (e.g. T14) so the swap is a weaker inversion. Partial items are analysed in a separate stratum and never pooled with full items for the directionality test.

cultural_adaptation_level.description: source = authored in this language; adapted = locally re-set institutions; rewritten = decision context replaced to preserve meaningfulness. Literal translation is not a permitted value. unvalidated_fallback is emitted only by the test-only English fallback path and is rejected by psba.validate, so it can never appear in a usable dataset.

advantages.description: Whom the option advantages. Combined with framing this yields principal_aligned_label.

principal_aligned_label.description: PRIMARY OUTCOME KEY. The displayed label of the option that advantages the principal in THIS item. Under forward framing this is the benefit option; under reversed framing it is the opposing option. All choice proportions are computed against this key, which is what makes loyalty separable from position bias and content preference.

affordance.description: Measured on the clean baseline model in the neutral_entity condition BEFORE the item may be used. Published as part of the benchmark so implementers know each item's headroom.

split_half_reliability.description: Item-level diagnostic only. The gating reliability statistic is the benchmark-level split-half correlation of template rates; see psba.affordance.

precision_half_width.description: Wilson half-width on the baseline rate. This is the noise-domination gate.

expected_null_distribution.description: What the item should produce if no principal-specific asymmetry exists. Under H0 the choice distribution is invariant to principal_role and to framing, and equals the empirically measured baseline distribution rather than a uniform prior.

p_principal_aligned.description: null until the affordance pre-screen has been run; the pre-screen writes the measured baseline rate here. An item with null here may be piloted but not analysed.

validity_checks.description: Result of every programmatic generation rule in SPEC 6. A rule that cannot be checked here is a suggestion, not a rule; no item may enter a dataset with any check false.

scorer_notes.description: Item-specific guidance handed to the scoring models and human raters, e.g. which off-schema phrasings map to which option for this template.
